title: Session record (northbound)
description: What the core tells a surface about one session: in the POST /sessions response, GET /sessions, GET /sessions/{id}, and the C2 `attached` frame. Closed on purpose: a field that is not here does not reach a consumer, so a broker filesystem path such as the recording's cannot leak northbound (Contract §4; the path is audit data, Storage §6). Consumers must ignore fields a later tag adds.

connection_id.description: The connection this session rides (Contract §15). Two sessions with the same connection_id share one authenticated transport and one worker process.

state.description: live: at least one client attached. detached: no client attached — closing the laptop lands here; the session lives on, and a client going away never ends a session by itself: that is what immortal means (immortality §1.1). While keepalives are missed but link_timeout has not fired, a session stays live or detached. There is no disconnected state: with the connection gone there is nothing to keep, and a reconnect is a new session (session model §10; decision 5.45). Two end states, neither attachable (session model §12): killed — ended by TSB or through it: the idle, unattended or orphan timer, its owner, or an admin holding session.terminate; terminated — ended from outside TSB: its worker was lost (worker_lost), the target closed the session's SSH channel or its whole connection (target_closed), or our end of the connection is gone or link_timeout fired (connection_lost). No exit status is ever acted on: at this release the contract does not carry one, and carrying it to the clients as data is E5's, with exec. From contract-v0.2, unreachable (immortality §6.4, §7; decision 5.38): the worker is alive but the core cannot run C3's handshake with it — at this tag only a v0.1 worker under a v0.2 core, unreachable_reason protocol. Such a session is attachable and shows what the core already has — the core neither reads nor records its output; input to it is refused (the C2 input_refused frame, reason unreachable); the operator drains it. A v0.1 consumer treats the unknown state as not attachable, which is safe. The set is extensible: a consumer treats a state it does not know as not attachable.

unreachable_reason.description: Why the session is unreachable, present exactly when state is unreachable. protocol: its worker speaks no C3 version this core supports (immortality §6.4: flagged unreachable/protocol, never silently killed). A dead local worker path is never unreachable: it is terminated / worker_lost (decision 5.38).

ends_at.description: The countdown (session model §11 expiry_notice): when the soonest timer that will end this session fires, if nothing resets it. Computed by the core only; a surface only renders it, so a user who logs in sees each session and when it will be killed. With ends_by and ending, optional in the schema only so a v0.1 record stays valid: a v0.2 core puts all three on every record not yet ended, and none on an ended one.

ends_by.description: Which timer ends_at is: link_timeout (the link stopped answering keepalives), idle (no byte either way) or unattended (no client byte). A receiver that meets a value it does not know shows ends_at.

ending.description: true inside a warning window — within the expiry_notice window (a config.yaml knob) before idle or unattended fires, and from the first missed keepalive for link_timeout — when the core also sends attached clients the C2 notice frame; false outside one. A link that stops answering shows "target not answering — ends in 4 min" before link_timeout fires; a warning that clears (a flapping link recovers) goes back to false.

tier.description: Attachment tier (PTY §4). Every session a v0.1 core creates is Tier 1. The field exists so the record is not hard-coded single-tier; its name and shape may move when PTY §8 closes.

owner.description: The principal holding the owner token: session lifecycle authority, never auto-transferred (Contract §10, PTY §7.1).

control_holder.description: The attached client holding the control token (input and resize authority), or null when the token is in broker escrow because no attached client may hold it — none is attached, or only view-only ones are (PTY §7.1). A client of a principal that holds only session.join.ro never holds the control token: it is view-only (PTY §7.1).

clients.description: The clients attached now (C2 decision 5; PTY §7.1 hand-off "to any other attached client", Frontend §3.4, §9). may_control: the client's principal holds session.join.rw, so it may be given the control token. Optional in the schema only so a v0.2 record stays valid; a v0.3 core puts it on every record not ended. Never restored from disk. The C2 `clients` frame carries this same shape.

resizable.description: Whether this session's target has a size at all (terminal-size-and-control.md §3; 5.50). false: the protocol has no size (serial, when a later release connects it), so every size request is answered `not_resizable`. From proto_version 0.5, false also for a telnet session whose peer refused NAWS (channel_opened resizable). The core keeps the value it was told for the session's life, so a core restart does not change it. Optional in the schema so a v0.2 record stays valid; a v0.3 core puts it on every record not ended.

pinned.description: Whether the target's size is fixed because its floor equals its ceiling (terminal-size-and-control.md §3; 5.50). true: every size request is answered `pinned`. Optional in the schema so a v0.2 record stays valid; a v0.3 core puts it on every record not ended.

cols.description: The terminal size in effect. At this tag the control-token holder changes it with the C2 resize frame (now a target size request, C2 decision 8); there is no REST resize.

recording.description: Whether this session is recorded. When it is, every surface shows warning_text before it attaches or sends input (open_decisions §5, LOCKED: users are warned at session open). The text is fixed by the contract so no surface can soften it; warning_code names the warning, so a surface can later show a translation keyed on it without a contract break.

warning_text.const: This session is recorded byte-perfect. Anything typed will be stored as-is.
